context.title: Abigail's Wise Appeal
context.summary: After Samuel's death, a rich man named Nabal insults David's request for food. David sets out for revenge, but Nabal's wise wife Abigail meets him with gifts and persuades him not to shed blood. God strikes Nabal down, and David marries Abigail.
context.background: Sheep-shearing was a festive time when owners were expected to be generous (compare 2 Samuel 13:23), and David's men had protected Nabal's shepherds (vv. 15–16). This Carmel is a town in Judah south of Hebron, not Mount Carmel. 'Nabal' means 'fool,' as Abigail says (v. 25).

customs.term: Bound in the bundle of life
customs.note: A picture of valuables tied up safely in a pouch, contrasted with stones slung away from a sling.

watchFor: The contrast between Nabal and Abigail (v. 3).
She foresees that God will make David 'a sure house' (v. 28).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Samuel
people.summary: Heard of God. The peculiar circumstances connected with his birth are recorded in 1 Sam. 1:20. Hannah, one of the two wives of Elkanah, who came up to Shiloh to worship before the Lord, earnestly prayed to God that she might become the mother of a son.

people.name: Caleb
people.summary: The son of Jephunneh (Num. 13:6; 32:12; Josh. 14:6, 14). He was one of those whom Moses sent to search the land in the second year after the Exodus.

people.name: Nabal
people.summary: Foolish, a descendant of Caleb who dwelt at Maon (1 Sam. 25), the modern Main, 7 miles south-east of Hebron. He was “very great, and he had 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats...but the man was churlish and evil in his doings.”

people.name: Abigail
people.summary: The wife of the churlish Nabal, who dwelt in the district of Carmel (1 Sam. 25:3). She showed great prudence and delicate management at a critical period of her husband’s life.

people.name: Jesse
people.summary: Firm, or a gift, a son of Obed, the son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:17, 22; Matt. 1:5, 6; Luke 3:32). He was the father of eight sons, the youngest of whom was David (1 Sam. 17:12).

people.name: Ahinoam
people.summary: A Jezreelitess, the first wife of David (1 Sam. 25:43; 27:3). She was the mother of Amnon (2 Sam. 3:2).

people.name: Saul
people.summary: The son of Kish (probably his only son, and a child of prayer, “asked for”), of the tribe of Benjamin, the first king of the Jewish nation. The singular providential circumstances connected with his election as king are recorded in 1 Sam. 8-10.

people.name: Michal
people.summary: Rivulet, or who as God?, the younger of Saul’s two daughters by his wife Ahinoam (1 Sam. 14:49, 50). “Attracted by the graces of his person and the gallantry of his conduct, she fell in love with David and became his wife” (18:20-28).

people.name: Phaltiel
people.summary: Deliverance of the Lord, the son of Laish of Gallim (1 Sam. 25:44)= Phaltiel (2 Sam. 3:15).

places.name: Paran
places.summary: Abounding in foliage, or abounding in caverns, (Gen. 21:21), a desert tract forming the north-eastern division of the peninsula of Sinai, lying between the ‘Arabah on the east and the wilderness of Shur on the west.

places.name: Ramah
places.summary: The same as Ramathaim-zophim, a town of Mount Ephraim (1 Sam. 1:1, 19).

places.name: Carmel
places.summary: A town in the hill country of Judah (Josh. 15:55), the residence of Nabal (1 Sam. 25:2, 5, 7, 40), and the native place of Abigail, who became David’s wife (1 Sam. 27:3).

places.name: Maon
places.summary: Habitation, a town in the tribe of Judah, about 7 miles south of Hebron, which gave its name to the wilderness, the district round the conical hill on which the town stood.

places.name: Jezreel
places.summary: A town in Judah (Josh. 15:56), to the south-east of Hebron.

places.name: Gallim
places.summary: Heaps, (1 Sam. 25:44; Isa. 10:30). The native place of Phalti, to whom Michal was given by Saul.

events.title: Reign of Saul
events.summary: Passage: 1 Samuel 10:1–31:2. People: Saul. Lasted about 40 years.
